sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The office has raised objection regarding maintainability of the appeal in the light of amendment of Section 173(2) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V.Act' for short) with effect from 09.08.2019, on the ground that the difference in the amount in dispute is less than Rs.1,00,000/-.
2. This appeal is arising out of judgment and award dated 13.09.2022 in MVC No.264/2020.
As per the award it is evident that the claimant has sought for compensation in a sum of Rs.8,50,000/- and the Tribunal has awarded compensation in a sum of Rs.25,000/-.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company has filed this appeal contending that since the rider of the offending vehicle was not possessing the valid driving licence, the Tribunal ought not to have fastened the liability on respondent No.2.
3.
Section 173(2) M.V.Act provides that no appeal shall lie against an award of a Claim Tribunal if the amount in dispute in the appeal is less than Rs.1,00,000/-.

Earlier this amount was Rs.10,000/-
and as per Act 32 of 2019, vide amendment of Section 57 of MV Act, with effect from 09.08.2019 (the date on which Presidential ascent is given and published in the gazette of India dated 09.08.2019), this limit is raised to Rs.1,00,000/-.
The present appeal is subsequent to the amendment.

Therefore, if the amount in dispute in the appeal is less than Rs.1,00,000/-, no appeal would lie.
4.

In this regard relying upon the following decisions, the learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the accident in respect of which appeal is filed is prior to the date of amendment and as the amendment is prospective nature, it is not applicable to the appeal in question:
i. State of Punjab and Others vs Bhajan Kaur and others1 (Bhajan Kaur's case) ii.
Sathy and others vs. Dileep and others2 (Sathy's case) Civil Appeal No.3406/2008 (arising out of SPL (Civil) No.12575/2008) OP (MAC) No.51/2022 dated 01.06.2022 5.

sentences.text: 2 compensation was enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that as per Section 92(A) of Act of 1939, the compensation payable under no fault liability was Rs.15,000/-.
It was raised to Rs.25,000/- vide Section 140 of the 1988 Act.
Again by Amending Act 54 of 1994, with effect from 14.11.1994, the quantum payable under no fault liability is increased to Rs.50,000/-.
Holding that the amendment is prospective in nature and as the accident in question is earlier to 14.11.1994, the claimants are not entitled for the said benefit.

6. So far as Sathy's case referred to supra is concerned, the accident was dated 23.05.2019 and based on Section 166(3) of the MV Act, which was a provision inserted by Section 53(iii) of the Act, 32 of 2019 with effect from 09.08.2019, the Tribunal had dismissed the claim petition summarily on the ground of limitation.

By observing that the amendment has come into effect on 09.08.2019 and as the accident is prior to the said date, the amendment is not applicable, the High Court set aside the dismissal order and remanded the matter.
7. Both the above decisions are not applicable to the case on hand, as they deal with different provision of the MV Act.

However, in the present case, the office objection is raised under Section 173(2) of the MV Act which prohibits entertaining an appeal against any award of a claims Tribunal if the amount in dispute is less than Rs.1,00,000/-.
So far as the appellant is concerned, the amount in dispute is Rs.25,000/- which is the compensation granted by the Tribunal.
Therefore, appeal is not maintainable.
Accordingly, the same is dismissed as not maintainable.
In view of dismissal of the appeal, IAs, if any, do not survive for consideration.
